authority_frontier: 1944-01-01T00:00 unchanged; authority revision v006 after Bengal rollback

Central_Pacific.US: Main Kwajalein/Roi-Namur D-Day succeeds on 6 Feb. Cabot remains campaign-out with return centered early May; Intrepid near-normal from 4 Feb. LST-224 is lost to Japanese submarine attack before D-Day; amphibious schedule absorbs the loss.
Central_Pacific.Japan: Shokaku/Zuikaku withdraw; Hiryu reaches Truk repair pipeline and is not a combat deck. Soryu readiness remains separate. Marshall local air ~21 serviceable by evening; one local conventional submarine lost and two boats mission-damaged/withdrawn, but reporting network not completely erased.

Indian_Ocean.state: No new event advanced in this Central-Pacific step. Eastern Fleet Ceylon workup continues; Japanese second surface reinforcement remains HOLD.

Bengal.state: No new post-year-end combat event advanced. After the v048 campaign rollback, Chittagong was captured centered late 14 Dec and 55th Division entered 1944 with about 300-600 more effective personnel and 20-45 more dispatchable vehicles than v001 implied. This hardens Japanese defenses and limited probes earlier, but Chittagong-Feni/Comilla stalemate persists; first Kinsei detachment remains and the further batch is held under Central-Pacific priority.

Yanagi_Jet.state: Clock is now inside I-34 projected early-Feb Europe-arrival band, but this Pacific step does not auto-realize arrival. It remains an unresolved near-term gate and must be adjudicated explicitly before jet-paper effects are applied.
